Messages.Author: Ke.
Messages.Body:
> ReverendRevolver wrote:
> All of those examples give you the rules. Now, practicality wise, know that the current player is done in thier minionphase. Say "tell me when your done with your minion phase" and or yell when they transfer.
>
Yes, there is an art to this also. Too early in their turn and you can give away your intentions; or beneficially induce them to pass the impulse (and end their minion phase) with the impression you're going to act. The best play depends on the situation — I think this is one of the less obvious strengths of Enkil Cog.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> thelonius wrote:
>
> > Lönkka wrote:
> > Also remember that after you take your Enkil Cog action, remember that impulse passes on to the player who's turn it is so, if they still have minions which ccould act, they can chose to do so.
> >
> If I give him the impulse, and he decline to act, may I act again?
>
No. You only get the impulse back if he does something.
It's the same thing in combat: if you declare no pre-maneuver, you give the impulse to the opposing minion. If he doesn't use it, combat moves to the maneuver step.
Or if you don't maneuver, you can't wait for the opponent to declare that he doesn't maneuver in order to play a maneuver.
